summary: Abridgment of Ch. II following the source's order and close third-person comic register. All eight verbatim excerpts are kept. The planted clues (Rita, Brown, the telephone message, the outer office, the Paris pensionnat, the ward role and the American accent) are left unexplained.
acceptable_changes: Compressed the opening assumption and some Lyons'/card exchanges, and cut the repeated 'At eleven o'clock?' lines.
Cut the post-office pen detail, the club-subscription aside and the vicarage line. Kept the wire text, the retained pencil and the ninepence-versus-five-shillings economy.
Cut the walk to the end of the street and the lift/stairs detail, and condensed the arrival to the top-floor door.
Cut the father/'gay deceiver' aside and trimmed Paris-offer exchanges. Some consecutive lines by the same speaker are merged.
Trimmed one round of 'quit fooling' and 'you insist on misjudging me' in the haggling. Kept three truthful replies and the double-bluff reasoning.
Cut the clock-time line and some of Whittington's ranting, including the 'details about your past life' rationale.
risks: Word count is estimated by hand and may sit slightly above the target range.
Some of Whittington's consecutive source lines are merged into single turns, for example the Paris/pensionnat answer and the 'perhaps it doesn't' rebuttal.
review_focus: Check that Brown appears only once, unremarked.
Check that the wire text and pencil survive for the Ch. III callback.
Check that the 'supper of buns' reference has its buns setup.
Check the transition from the dream to the next-morning arrival at the office.
